translationRepairs: Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li Cheng, Han, Lu, and Gao
Cui, Deng, Wei, Wei, Li, Han, Lu, and Gao
Chinese 崔鄧魏衛李韓盧高 lists surnames only; 李 has no given name, so idiomatic Li Cheng invents Cheng and the proposed surname-only list is correct.
When rebel bands raided Jingyang, Zhang Xiu sacrificed in a shrine, slaughtered oxen, and feasted with loud shouting.
When rebel bands raided Jingyang, they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen, and feasted with loud shouting.
休祠房 means the rebels rested in the shrine halls; 休 is the verb ‘rest,’ not a person Zhang Xiu. Context (賊醉) confirms the rebels themselves were drinking there.
It happened rebel bands raided Jingyang; Xiu sacrificed in a shrine, pounded oxen and shouted drinking.
It happened rebel bands raided Jingyang; they rested in a shrine building, slaughtered oxen and shouted while drinking.
The literal likewise turns 休 into a name ‘Xiu’ and misreads 椎牛; ‘they rested… slaughtered oxen and shouted while drinking’ matches 休祠房，椎牛呼飲.
Before long, Songzhou prefect Liu Dian rebelled.
Before long, Songzhou prefect Liu Zhan rebelled.
s0045’s 劉殿 is the same rebel whom s0046–s0047 name 展; English Liu Dian is wrong, and Liu Zhan restores the co-referent name.
Wang Silun was at Taiyuan with granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half the stores to fill the capital.
Wang Sili was at Taiyuan with granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half the stores to fill the capital.
王思禮 is Wang Sili (思禮); Silun is an unsupported reading, and the rest of the proposed idiomatic matches the Chinese.
Wang Silun was at Taiyuan; granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half to fill the capital.
Wang Sili was at Taiyuan; granaries full and overflowing; he requested shipping half to fill the capital.
The literal has the same Silun error for 王思禮; Wang Sili is the correct personal name and the remainder is unchanged.
The deputy commander Zang Jie and the judicial officer Dazi Gun quarreled in anger; Gun said, "We are fortunate to have no trouble now."
The deputy commander Zang Jie and the judicial officer Daxi Gou quarreled in anger; Gou said, "We are fortunate to have no trouble now."
達奚覯 is the compound surname Daxi plus given name Gou; Dazi Gun misreads both the surname and 覯, and the proposed dialogue attribution to Gou is correct.
He flung his robe and left; that night he killed Gun with troops.
He flung his robe and left; that night he killed Gou with troops.
是夜以兵殺覯 names the victim 覯 (Gou); continuing Gun from the prior misreading is wrong, and the proposed idiomatic corrects only that name.
Li Cheng led troops intending to take Bian, camped at its north gate and dared not advance; when Liu He's army camped at the east gate, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen surrendered to him.
Li Cheng led troops intending to take Bian, camped at its north gate and dared not advance; when Liu Qia's army camped at the east gate, the rebel general Tian Huaizhen surrendered to him.
劉洽 is Liu Qia (洽); Liu He invents an unsupported given name, and the proposed idiomatic corrects only that personal name.
Liu He stationed troops on the border and sent envoys to instruct him to stop; Kening then restrained himself, yet the roads remained closed for half a month.
Liu Qia stationed troops on the border and sent envoys to instruct him to stop; Kening then restrained himself, yet the roads remained closed for half a month.
s0105 again has 劉洽; Liu Qia matches 洽, and the rest of the proposed idiomatic is unchanged.

At first Shence commandant Tuoba Chenghuan was encamped opposite him; Congshi would visit his camp to drink and gamble, and Chenghuan often produced precious belts and curious objects to show off to him.

At first Shence commandant Tutu Chengcui was encamped opposite him; Congshi would visit his camp to drink and gamble, and Chengcui often produced precious belts and curious objects to show off to him.
吐突承璀 is Tutu Chengcui, not Tuoba Chenghuan; the proposed idiomatic restores the correct surname and given name while leaving the rest intact.

In the Yuanhe era, as left Weiwu guard general he followed Tuoba Chenghuan to attack Wang Chengzong; many generals lost their armies, but Xiayu alone distinguished himself, and an edict stored the armor and weapons he captured in the Shence arsenal to honor him.

In the Yuanhe era, as left Weiwu guard general he followed Tutu Chengcui to attack Wang Chengzong; many generals lost their armies, but Xiayu alone distinguished himself, and an edict stored the armor and weapons he captured in the Shence arsenal to honor him.
隨吐突承璀 again names Tutu Chengcui; replacing Tuoba Chenghuan with Tutu Chengcui corrects only that error.
He was nominally demoted to prefect of Guizhou.
By edict he was demoted to prefect of Guizhou.
Chapter 詒貶 is a graphic corruption of 詔貶; an edition reading 詔貶歸州刺史 supports demotion by edict, not a ‘nominal’ demotion.
He was falsely demoted to Prefect of Guizhou.
By edict he was demoted to Prefect of Guizhou.
Literal ‘falsely’ follows corrupt 詒; the same external 詔貶歸州刺史 reading justifies ‘By edict he was demoted to Prefect of Guizhou.’
Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Kuanshan in the Sui dynasty.
Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Pushan in the Sui dynasty.
隋蒲山公寬 is Duke Kuan of Pushan (蒲山), not Kuanshan; the proposed idiomatic corrects only that place/title name.
Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Kuanshan in the Sui dynasty.
Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a distant descendant of Duke Kuan of Pushan in the Sui dynasty.
The literal likewise has Kuanshan for 蒲山; Pushan matches the Chinese, and the rest of the proposed literal is unchanged.
